scope: Only test/45_task3_repeat_dropout may be created or modified. Experiment 44, production code, other experiments, and existing checkpoints must remain unchanged. This preregistration is frozen before any experiment-45 real-data fit, inference, or metric.

background.classifier: The v5 Task3 classifier is trained on real public single trials; experiment 22's added three-repeat mean rows did not establish a useful improvement.
background.question: While retaining every permitted real single trial exactly once per epoch, does the one fixed count-dropout candidate improve pre-assignment candidate recall without sacrificing final OCF relative to a freshly paired no-augmentation baseline?
background.not_a_repeat_of_mean_augmentation: No classifier mean rows, duplicated rows, trial averaging, repeat-mean inference, logit ensembling, or new fusion weights are introduced. Existing v5 ridge prototypes remain a shared, unchanged encoding component and are fitted only from permitted train_trials.

data_and_split.data_scope: public train only; load_feature_blocks(DATA, 'train', bin_ms=50); no competition test file, hidden label, hidden ID, or submission is read
data_and_split.normalizer: For each block independently, fit_session_normalizer uses only its raw train_trials. The identical fitted normalizer is shared by baseline and candidate and applied after any candidate raw-count thinning. Validation responses never affect normalization.
data_and_split.classifier_feature_normalization: SpikeClassifier.set_normalization is fitted on the original, session-normalized train_trials matrix, identically for both arms; thinned rows never change these statistics.
data_and_split.label_use: Public train labels fit the classifier and shared ridge encoding. Validation target IDs are used only to verify gallery completeness, select the frozen reporting subsets after full-block ranking/assignment, and compute metrics. They never enter scores, thinning, unique_assignment, training, or checkpoint selection.
data_and_split.integrity_assertions: Require disjoint train/validation trial indices, exactly three training rows and one validation row per glyph per block, complete validation galleries, in-range labels, finite nonnegative integer raw counts, identical raw train rows/targets/order across arms, and label-independent score ranking and assignment.

picture_subsets.tune: sort(order[:256]); 256 glyph IDs per block, 2048 rows across eight blocks
picture_subsets.heldout: sort(order[256:768]); 512 glyph IDs per block, 4096 rows across eight blocks
picture_subsets.historical_reuse_disclosure: These IDs were used by earlier local experiments and are not pristine confirmatory data. No result-dependent change to p, seeds, epochs, architecture, gates, or subsets is allowed in this experiment.

fixed_training_contract.seed_lock: Only seed 42 is fitted for each mouse and arm. No seed may be added, removed, replaced, reordered, or selected after seeing results. Deterministic augmentation and row-order streams are derived from seed 42 and epoch number and are not additional training seeds.
fixed_training_contract.checkpoint: fixed final epoch; no early stopping, validation-based checkpointing, or best-epoch selection
fixed_training_contract.optimizer: AdamW(lr=0.0003, weight_decay=0.001), fused only when device is CUDA
fixed_training_contract.row_order: For each arm and mouse independently, epoch e (1-based) uses numpy.random.default_rng(42 + e).permutation(n_train_rows); baseline and candidate therefore receive exactly the same row order.
fixed_training_contract.torch_randomness: Call torch.manual_seed(42) before model construction and again before the first training epoch for each mouse-arm. Model initialization and architectural Dropout use the same seed and call pattern in both arms. Candidate count noise uses NumPy only and cannot advance the Torch RNG.
fixed_training_contract.paired_training: Each mouse-arm is constructed and trained independently with the same raw rows, normalized rows, targets, row orders, initial seed, architecture, optimizer, epoch count, and final-epoch rule. The sole training difference is the candidate's frozen raw-count perturbation.

frozen_count_dropout_candidate.baseline: Every original real single-trial count row is used unchanged once per epoch.
frozen_count_dropout_candidate.candidate_row_probability: For every training row and epoch independently, draw u ~ Bernoulli(0.5). If u=1, preserve the complete original raw count row exactly. If u=0, replace that row for this presentation by independent elementwise Binomial(n=x_ij, p=0.5) thinning.
frozen_count_dropout_candidate.p_frozen_without_search: Both probabilities are fixed at 0.5 before real training. There is no p grid, internal repeat-fold p selection, tune-based p selection, heldout-based p selection, or post-hoc repair. Testing another value requires a separately preregistered experiment.
frozen_count_dropout_candidate.normalization_order: raw integer counts -> optional frozen thinning -> shared train-only session log1p normalization -> original-train-fitted SpikeClassifier feature normalization
frozen_count_dropout_candidate.scaling: No inverse-p scaling, count restoration, offset, clipping beyond the existing normalizers, or other compensation.
frozen_count_dropout_candidate.augmentation_rng: Within each mouse candidate fit and epoch e, initialize numpy.random.default_rng(1042 + e). Draw the preserve-original mask for each batch in the frozen row order, then draw Binomial counts only for non-preserved rows. Batch size and loop order are fixed, making the stream reproducible.
frozen_count_dropout_candidate.row_count: No extra rows: each real training single trial appears exactly once per epoch in both arms. Across epochs a candidate row may be original or freshly thinned; all original source rows remain available and are never overwritten.
frozen_count_dropout_candidate.inference: No count noise, preserve/drop sampling, mean trial, repeat aggregation, test-time augmentation, or logit averaging. Both classifiers use model.eval() and the original validation single-trial counts. Existing architectural Dropout is disabled by eval mode.

frozen_v5_scoring.shared_encoding: Per mouse, fit RidgePath on bank_coefficients[train_targets] versus log1p(per-glyph means of the three permitted raw training repeats), pooled over its four blocks; predict all glyph prototypes with alpha=0.01. This is the unchanged v5 encoding control and is identical across arms. No validation trial enters it.
frozen_v5_scoring.score: For each arm and complete validation block: (row_zscore(MLP logits) + row_zscore(response_scores(log1p(raw), prototypes, metric='mse')) + row_zscore(continuous_image_scores)) / 3.
frozen_v5_scoring.continuous_image_scores: The existing v5 fixed T=1 softmax expectation over centered DCT16 gallery coefficients, L2-normalized expected image and gallery, followed by cosine similarity.
frozen_v5_scoring.pre_assignment: Before unique_assignment, rank all 2748 glyph scores per validation row with stable descending argsort and ascending glyph-ID tie breaking. Recall@1 uses the first ranked glyph; recall@32 uses membership in the first min(32, n_glyphs) ranked glyphs.
frozen_v5_scoring.final_assignment: Apply scipy-backed src.retrieval.unique_assignment independently to every complete 2748 x 2748 arm/block score matrix using scores only. Only after full-gallery one-to-one assignment are tune or heldout rows selected.
frozen_v5_scoring.final_ocf: Official src.evaluation.score_predictions OCF for the assigned glyph versus the true public glyph; cache is shared across arms and subsets and keyed only by (assigned_id, target_id).
frozen_v5_scoring.reporting: Report recall@1, recall@32, assigned-ID accuracy, and final OCF overall, separately for mice1 and mice2, and separately for all eight blocks. Candidate-minus-baseline paired deltas use identical rows. Recall@1 and recall@32 remain distinct from final assignment outcomes.

frozen_gates.tune_gate: Evaluate both arms on tune only. For EACH mouse separately require candidate recall@32 >= baseline recall@32 AND candidate final OCF >= baseline final OCF. Both mice and both conditions must pass. Overall and eight-block values are reported but are not alternative gates.
frozen_gates.tune_failure_stop: If any tune condition fails, save tune metrics and stop: do not select/evaluate heldout rows or compute heldout OCF. Full-block unlabeled score/assignment matrices needed for tune may contain other rows, but no heldout metric or label-based comparison is produced.
frozen_gates.heldout_gate: Only after the tune gate passes, evaluate the same two frozen arms on heldout. For EACH mouse separately require candidate recall@32 strictly > baseline recall@32 AND candidate final OCF >= baseline final OCF. All four conditions must pass.
frozen_gates.decision: advance=true only if both tune and heldout gates pass. Any failure stops with advance=false. No tolerance, post-hoc metric substitution, subset/block omission, p change, seed change, epoch change, or extra candidate is permitted.
frozen_gates.production: No production integration or hidden-test submission is performed by this experiment even if advance=true; a pass only justifies separate review.

expected_real_compute_scale.calculation: 2 mice x 2 arms x 7 epochs x ceil(32976/256) batches
expected_real_compute_scale.note: Counts describe computational volume only; no runtime prediction is made.
